{{Short description|Swedish professor of biochemistry}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2022}}
{{refimprove|date=October 2025}}
'''Pål Nyrén''' (born 1955{{citation needed lead|date=October 2025}}) was, as of June 2009, a [[biochemistry]] professor at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] (KTH), [[Stockholm]].{{update after|2025|10|28}}<!--Cannot make a statement regarding present reality based on an archived 2009 source.--><ref name= 2009KTHautobio/>{{third party inline|date=October 2025}} He is known for having developed the [[pyrosequencing]] method for [[DNA sequencing]].{{says who|date=October 2025}}{{citation needed lead|date=October 2025}}<!--Phrase "most famous" deleted as editorialising, as the sentence is currently unsourced. Note, in re: citations: The two papers appearing here earlier were Nyrén primary sources (now moved to Further reading). One can't establish primacy of discovery, citing research by the purported discoverer. (!) Independent secondary sources are unequivocally required.-->

==Early life and education==
{{third party|section|date=October 2025}}
Pål Nyrén was born 1955.{{where|date=October 2025}}{{cn|date=October 2025}} After undergraduate training,{{what|date=October 2025}}{{where|date=October 2025}} he received an [[M.S.]] in Chemical Engineering, in 1981, from the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] (KTH), in [[Stockholm|Stockholm, Sweden]].<ref name= 2009KTHautobio>{{cite web | author = Nyrén, Pål | date = 2009-01-23 | title= Pål Nyrén | work = KTH Biotechnology, Division of Biochemistry (Biotech.KTH.se) | format = employment autobiography | url=http://www.biotech.kth.se/biochem/nyren/ | access-date=2010-05-10 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090629050203/http://www.biotech.kth.se/biochem/nyren/ | archive-date=29 June 2009 }}{{third party inline|date=October 2025}}</ref>{{third party inline|date=October 2025}} He then completed a [[Ph.D.]] in Biochemistry, at the University of Stockholm, in 1985,<ref name= 2009KTHautobio/>{{third party inline|date=October 2025}} with a dissertation entitled, "The Proton Pumping Pyrophosphatase From ''Rhodospirillum rubrum''."{{cn|date=October 2025}} He did a post-doctoral fellowship under [[John E. Walker|John Walker]]{{verification needed|date=October 2025}}<!--Needed is verification that it was this John Walker, and not another, at the MRC, that Nyrén worked under. Beside being autobiographical, the only source we have, Nyrén's old faculty page, does not state the middle initial that this MRC Walker regularly used.--> at the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|MRC]]'s [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] in [[Cambridge, England]], from 1985-1986.<ref name= 2009KTHautobio/>{{third party inline|date=October 2025}}

==Career==
{{third party|section|date=October 2025}}
As Nyrén has stated at his faculty web page (as of June 2009),{{update after|2025|10|28}}, he has held the following academic posts:<blockquote>"1988 Associate [[professor]] (Docent) Biochemistry [[Stockholm University|University of Stockholm]]"[;]<br>"1999 Professor in Biochemistry, KTH, Stockholm"[.]<ref name= 2009KTHautobio/>{{third party inline|date=October 2025}}</blockquote>

He also lists himself as "[f]ounder of the company Biotage AB (former [[Pyrosequencing]] AB)" in 1997,<ref name= 2009KTHautobio/>{{third party inline|date=October 2025}} which is more accurately stated as his participating in the founding of a pyrosequencing unit, with other academics at [[Royal Institute of Technology|KTH]], a unit once a part of the complex set of businesses of Biotage AB created through [[mergers and acquisitions]], with that pyrosequencing unit having been sold off to [[Qiagen]] in 2008.<ref>In detail, Biotage AB actually arose, per its company description, from a series of events beginning with the 1969 founding by Colin Jones of [[Jones Chromatography]] (in Wales); the much later (1989) founding by [[Sheridan Snyder]] of [[Biotage LLC]] for "systems for drug discovery and purification" in the U.S.; the 1994 foundings of [[Argonaut Technologies]] by [[Larry Bock]] and [[Joel Martin]] in the U.S. and of [[Personal Chemistry]] (originally [[Labwell]]), in [[Stockholm, Sweden]] (a [[Microwave chemistry|microwave synthesis]] startup), by [[Sharon Stone-Elander]] and [[Sören Nygren]]; the 1997 founding of [[Pyrosequencing AB]], in [[Uppsala, Sweden]], "specializing in developing instruments for sequencing DNA strands and building on technique developed at The Royal Institute of Technology, KTH, Stockholm" (with Stockholm [[IPO]], 2000); the 2000 founding of [[MIP Technologies]] in [[Lund, Sweden]] by [[Christine Berggren]] and [[Kees Ensing]]; Argonaut's acquisition of Jones in 2002, Pyrosequencing's acquisitions of Biotage and Personal Chemistry in 2003, and the renaming of the conglomerate as Biotage AB at that time. Biotage AB went on to acquire Argonaut in 2005 and MIP in 2010, the latter only after, in 2008, having sold to [[Qiagen]] the "biosystems branch of Biotage AB and the Pyrosequencing brand" (the latter the unit possibly co-founded by title subject Pål Nyrén,{{third party inline|date=October 2025}} and [[Mostafa Ronaghi]] [in re: the latter, see Bornstein & Illumina (4 August 2008), op. cit.]). ''Note, see Biotage Staff (28 October 2025), op. cit.: the name "Pål Nyrén" does not appear on the [[Biotage AB]] history page, despite that page being rich with the names of founders of Biotage's component businesses.'' 
:This historical summary is otherwise drawn entirely from {{cite web | author = Biotage Staff | date = 28 October 2025 | title = Our History: Spanning Five Decades | work = Biotage.com | url = https://www.biotage.com/biotage-history | access-date = 28 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release | author = Bornstein, Maurissa & Illumina Staff | date = 4 August 2008 | title =  News Release: Illumina Appoints Mostafa Ronaghi as Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer | work = Illumina.com | url = http://investor.illumina.com/phoenix.zhtml?c=121127&p=irol-newsArticle&ID=1182777&highlight= | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20081003144414/http://investor.illumina.com/phoenix.zhtml?c=121127&p=irol-newsArticle&ID=1182777&highlight= | archive-date = 2008-10-03 | location = San Diego, CA | publisher = Illumina, Inc. | via = Business Wire | quote = In 1997, [Mostafa Ronaghi] co-founded Pyrosequencing AB, which was later renamed to Biotage AB in 2003, and led the company to a successful initial public offering in June 2000 on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2013, Nyrén was awarded the [[European Patent Office]]'s [[European Inventor Award]], in the SMEs category.{{what|date=October 2025}}<ref>{{cite web | title=Lighting up the code of life | url=http://www.epo.org/learning-events/european-inventor/finalists/2013/nyren/feature.html }}</ref>
